Teach her these 10 things before the world does. 👑

Chloe is five. Every night her mom tells her she's a daughter of the King. Then, year by year:
1️⃣ Know her worth. Love isn't something she has to beg for.
2️⃣ Use her voice. "That's not fair!"
3️⃣ Be kind, without people-pleasing. Kindness is a gift, not a debt.
4️⃣ Stand on her own. 🚲
5️⃣ Don't chase popularity. She's more than fitting in.
6️⃣ Walk away from disrespect, even from friends who laugh at her.
7️⃣ Let failure teach her. Not making the team doesn't mean she's a failure.
8️⃣ Protect her boundaries. "No." means no.
9️⃣ Live the life God made her for. Her worth is given, not earned.
🔟 Never make herself small for the wrong people.

Research shows that by age six, girls are already less likely than boys to think people of their gender can be "really, really smart" (Bian, Leslie & Cimpian, Science, 2017). 💔

Jesus wore a crown of thorns so she could wear hers. 🙏 "See what kind of love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God; and so we are." 1 John 3:1

At sixteen, when someone tries to tell her who she is, she just smiles. She already knew. ❤️
